searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's; the shared appellation search counted with Orealios Gaea. Six were restricted to a producer's or a wine body's domain (gentilini.gr twice, sclavoswines.gr twice, haritatosvineyard.com twice, winesofgreece.org twice) and read as primary for the house's own facts. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on no source was cut; sources whose address names a living critic were met and are not cited.

tested: Wild Paths: 850 metres, the oldest vineyard, poor rocky limestone, ungrafted bush vines, the half and half yeast split, a fifth in French and American oak, four months of batonnage: gentilini.gr Wild Paths page and its 2019 sheet (two searches on the house's domain), Botilia; kept, bush vines added.
The Venetian engineer and Assos in 1593, the 1978 planting, the 1984 first vintage in Athens and London, the second generation in 2002: gentilini.gr About and a trade catalogue; kept.
The Cellar Selection: Falstaff 2010 and CellarTracker 2012 listings show it existed; no source says Wild Paths replaced it; the succession claim cut.
changed: wine.sites: ungrafted bush vines added, by the house's Wild Paths page and its technical sheet of 2019.

story: was that Wild Paths took the place of the Cellar Selection at the head of the range, on one guide; now the older Robola Cellar Selection is told as sold into the early 2010s (Falstaff's 2010 and CellarTracker's 2012 listings) and no longer in the range, with no claim that one succeeded the other.
others: the classic Robola was said to be made in steel with weeks of lees stirring, unsourced; now from the house's vineyards on Mount Ainos inside the zone, by the house's Robola page.
open: The wine name still carries the words once the Robola Cellar Selection only so it lints against the plan; when the read-together agent applies the swap to Robola Wild Paths, the name becomes Robola Wild Paths alone.
Founded 1984 is the first vintage; a trade catalogue gives 1978, the first planting, as the founding. The record keeps 1984 and tells 1978 in the story.
Botilia names the 850 metre vineyard as Fagia; the house's own pages do not, so Fagia stays out for want of a second source.

tested: Odessa, 1860, 1919 and Kechrion: Greek Gastronomy Guide, Greeka, Raisin; the 1700 settling conflicts and is cut.

Vino di Sasso: 650 to 700 metres, about thirty year old vines, broken limestone, long extraction, alcoholic and malolactic fermentation by native yeasts, Napier and the name: sclavoswines.gr products page (two searches on the house's domain).
Demeter: covers the family's own vines, the bought fruit organic, by a critic's site that cannot be cited; the Demeter claims on the wine cut.
1990 against 1995, Orgion and Monampele, Metagitnion of old ungrafted Vostilidi: the house, the guide, Cream Wine Company.
changed: wine.making, table, label, questions: was grown and certified by Demeter with a small addition of sulphur, and a label term and a question on the Demeter mark; the Demeter certification covers the family's own vines while the Robola zone lies on Mount Ainos far from Kechrion, and the sulphur had no source; now the house's own account of the making, a long extraction with alcoholic and malolactic fermentation completed by native yeasts (sclavoswines.gr products page), the Demeter label term replaced by PDO and the wine question set on the fermentation.
wine.sites: now about thirty year old vines on broken limestone under Mount Ainos, by the house's products page.

story, question: was a branch settled in Odessa around 1700, one source against others; now the branch traded from Odessa, with the wine business of about 1860, by the house and the Greek Gastronomy Guide.

story: was the vineyard remade from 1990 with Mavrodaphne and Vostilidi planted and among the first biodynamic estates in Greece; the house gives 1990 and the guide 1995, and the house's own Vostilidi comes from vines of more than ninety years; now the vineyard remade in the 1990s, organic then biodynamic farming, the family's own vines certified by Demeter, with no claim of a first.

others: Sclavos Vostilidi and Sclavos Mavrodaphne are not label names; now Metagitnion, the house's Vostilidi from old ungrafted vines (sclavoswines.gr), and Orgion, its Mavrodaphne of Cephalonia (Cream Wine Company, Shrine to the Vine).
cards: the name card now says the house credits the name to a British official, as the story tells it.
open: The year of the Demeter certification, 2019, and that the fruit the house buys is organic rest on a critic's site whose address names a living writer, so neither is told.
The Napier of the house's account is not named: the house does not give his full name, and the likely Charles James Napier was not confirmed as the man it means.

tested: 1982 by about three hundred growers, the winery completed in 1987 with state help beside Saint Gerasimos, 2005 renewal: Wines of Greece, Maltby and Greek, Greece and Grapes, a naturist Kefalonia guide; bought corrected to completed.
PDO 1982, 175 to 800 metres, Omala and the slopes of Ainos: Wines of Greece (search on its domain).
Robola in steel, oxidation, medium body, honeyed ageing over three or four years: Wines of Greece variety page; light body corrected.
San Gerasimo: Botilia, Greece and Grapes; lees and low yields one source each, cut.
changed: story, cards, question: was that the co-operative bought a winery in 1987; now its own winery was completed in 1987 with state help, beside the monastery of Saint Gerasimos (naturist Kefalonia guide, Greece and Grapes, the Greek Foundation).
story, card: the founders, said to be the growers of Omala, are now about three hundred of the island's growers (Maltby and Greek, Passport Nomads).
wine.glass: was light in body with a short finish; Wines of Greece gives Robola medium body and short was unsourced; now medium in body with a clean finish.
table: the Robola most lists carry was a market claim; now told through the growers who gather most of the island's Robola (Wines of Greece, Maltby and Greek).
others, story: San Gerasimo's low yields and fine lees rest on one shop each; now a selection from higher, semi mountain vineyards, chosen year by year.
open: The co-operative publishes no sheet of the plain Robola; the making follows the national wine body's account of the variety.

tested: 1863 farmhouse at Kladata, in the family since 1863, Hariton for the grandfather, perhaps the first pure Vostylidi bottled for sale: haritatosvineyard.com (search on its domain).
PGI Slopes of Aenos: Skurnik and Greece and Grapes; kept. The PGI dates from 1997 by Wines of Greece.
Typaldo and the Venetian ancestor: the house's Typaldo page gives the older name Typaldos Haritatos, no Venetian; corrected.
Muscat and the wine press: Greeka is garbled on Muscat; cut.
changed: story: was a Venetian ancestor of the family; no source names one, and the house's Typaldo page speaks of the family's older name, Typaldos Haritatos; now so told.

story: Muscat among the house's grapes and the old wine press become a winery rest on no clear source; cut. The church is now a chapel, with medicinal plants among the olives, by the house's estate page and Greeka.

others: Mademoiselle Haritatou was said to open a new way with the grape, unsourced; now the family's dry red Mavrodaphne. Typaldo was said to be named for a Venetian ancestor; now it recalls the family's older name, by the house.
open: The Greek Gastronomy Guide dates the estate's bottled wine from 2012, one source, so founded stays empty and no first vintage of Hariton is given.

tested: Melissinos renamed Petrakopoulos, at Thiramonas, since 2002, Robola, Mavrodaphne and Zakynthino: Decanter, Greece and Grapes, Botilia, Monocle; kept.
Robola Natural Palia Armakia as the successor of Melissinos Robola Natural (2015, 2016): Botilia, Greece and Grapes, Decantalo; Orina Armakia cut.
Thymari Petras, Lakkomatia, about 600 metres, thyme: Botilia and a second listing; added.
changed: story, card: the natural Robola was said to appear as Palia Armakia and Orina Armakia; only Palia Armakia is labelled Robola Natural (Botilia, Greece and Grapes), so Orina Armakia is cut.
others: Thymari Petras now from the Lakkomatia hillside at about 600 metres, named for the thyme among the vines (Botilia and a second listing).
open: The swap to Petrakopoulos with Robola Natural Palia Armakia is accepted; the read-together agent applies it to plan.json, with a new key, and then the producer, the wine name and the say of this record follow it.
Spontaneous fermentation with little sulphur rests on one shop and a critic's site naming a living writer, so the making stays thin.

livingNamesMet: The founder of Gentilini, his daughter and her husband (named in the house's pages and a catalogue).
The three Haritatos siblings who run the estate (named on the house's estate page).
The founder of the Petrakopoulos winery (named by Decanter and Greece and Grapes).
The living winemaker of Sclavos (named by Raisin).
None is named in the fragment; the merge or read-together agent may add them to people.json.

swaps.why: The Cellar Selection is found only in listings of 2010 and 2012 and is not in the house's range; Wild Paths is the house's single vineyard Robola from its oldest vines, on its own pages. The key may stay gentilini if the read-together agent judges a changed wine on one producer needs no new key; otherwise a new key.

The winery trades as Petrakopoulos by Decanter, Greece and Grapes and Botilia, and its natural Robola is labelled Robola Natural Palia Armakia by two shops; a guest will meet that name. The alternative of Sarris is refused: no search here tested it, and the winery picked is real and still makes the wine.

codexTension: The region summary speaks of Robola as lemon, flint and smoke; Wines of Greece speaks of delicate citrus and salinity, and the records follow the national body. Reported, not edited.
